judged_text: createEvent now resolves the target calendar only via `destinationCalendar.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, so a destination calendar whose credentialId is null never matches and the event is created on 'primary' instead of the configured calendar. Bookings for users whose DestinationCalendar rows have null credentialId (the legacy rows the EventManager's filter-by-integration fallback branch exists to serve) silently land on the account's primary calendar; the user's selected destination calendar never receives the event, where the old `destinationCalendar?.externalId` code targeted it correctly.

Bookings for users whose DestinationCalendar rows have null credentialId (the legacy rows the EventManager's filter-by-integration fallback branch exists to serve) silently land on the account's primary calendar; the user's selected destination calendar never receives the event, where the old `destinationCalendar?.externalId` code targeted it correctly.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `createEvent` now selects the target calendar solely via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId` and falls back to `"primary"` when no match (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). In `packages/core/EventManager.ts#createAllCalendarEvents`, the legacy branch explicitly handles destinations with no `credentialId` by selecting credentials by `destination.integration` and calling `createEvent(c, event)` (no externalId passed and the destination objects may have `credentialId` null/undefined). For such legacy `DestinationCalendar` rows, GoogleCalendarService will not find a matching `credentialId`, so `selectedCalendar` becomes undefined and the event is inserted into the primary calendar instead of the configured `destination.externalId` (which the old `destinationCalendar.externalId` logic would have used).
